messages:
maria: heads up: saw 3x tail latency for private-eu clusters starting ~08:50 UTC, correlates with large KV cache miss bursts and SNAT error spikes :rotating_light:
simon: link to the dashboard?
maria: https://redwood.internal/perf/dashboards/cluster-private-eu — look at p95/p99 tokens and the SNAT port exhaustion graph (ports/sec). big step at 08:50.
akshay: grabbing perf traces now. running perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30 on one of affected nodes
leo: packet capture on the NAT box shows lots of fragmented packets and frequent ICMP frag-needed replies: sudo tcpdump -nn -s0 -w /tmp/egress_frag.pcap 'host 10.0.2.45 and not port 22'
maria: interesting — we rolled a kernel selector change yesterday that pushes small-packet path to the generic reassembly kernel when MTU mismatch detected. might be falling back too aggressively.
infra-bot: deploy: kernel-selector v2.3 promoted to private-eu at 02:13 UTC yesterday
simon: akshay, any hotspots from perf?
akshay: userspace shows a bunch of time in skb_frag_copy and ip_defrag. flamegraph attached (brief): lots of cycles in nf_conntrack and iptable NAT chains. KV cache RPCs waiting ~30-50ms more when fragmentation happens.
leo: firewall rules also show an extra mangle/POSTROUTING rule we added for egress tagging — that adds one extra lookup; with conntrack churn it's amplifying.
jess: tagging rule was added for billing; should be no-op but might increase hash collisions if conntrack table near cap. current conntrack count ~ 420k / max 524k.
maria: hypothesis: MTU on customer VPNs dropped (PMTU change) causing servers to fragment, kernel-selector fallback to defrag-heavy path, conntrack churn + SNAT port reuse -> per-request retry and batching backpressure.
simon: can we reproduce with iperf from a canary app? set MTU 1400 on a canary host and run a KV load.
akshay: repro confirmed: with MTU 1400, p99 latency climbs 2.8x and we see fragmentation + nf_conntrack CPU spike.
leo: quick mitigation suggestions?
jess: immediate: 1) adjust sysctl net.ipv4.netfilter.ip_conntrack_max to +20% on affected NAT nodes 2) enable mss_clamp on vpn-facing interface to avoid fragmentation 3) temp rollback kernel-selector to v2.2 which prefers small-packet optimized path
maria: +1 for mss_clamp and conntrack bump. For kernel rollback we need a canary first.
ops-bot: runbook applied: increased conntrack max on nat-01/02/03, enabled mss_clamp on vpn0 via ansible.
simon: changed batching heuristics in runtime to reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 for private-eu (hotfix) to lower amplification during retries. Deployed to 10% of pods.
akshay: perf after mss_clamp + conntrack bump: nf_conntrack CPU down ~60%, fragmentation ICMP gone, p99 latency back to baseline on canary.
maria: leaving kernel-selector rollback pending — we'll roll v2.2 to 20% and monitor. schedule postmortem and longer-term fixes: conntrack hashing better spread, add SNAT port range expansion, and make kernel-selector threshold less aggressive (only fallback after 3 successive defrag events).
leo: also file to audit mangle/POSTROUTING rules; if tagging can be moved to a sidecar we avoid penalty on fast path.
jess: created ticket INF-4829 for postmortem + followups.
infra-bot: note: rollback scheduled (kernel-selector v2.2) canary at 09:40 UTC
maria: thanks all — will keep thread updated. please drop any stray logs here. :thumbsup:
